Photograph: Jay L Clendenin/Getty Images Donald Trump Man arrested at Trump’s California golf course faces more charges Jeanine John Taele detained for ‘suspicious’ behavior and charged with possession of unregistered short-barreled rifle Uwa Ede-Osifo and agency Wed 5 Aug 2026 19.02 EDT First published on Wed 5 Aug 2026 18.28 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A California man who was arrested at Donald Trump ’s Los Angeles-area golf course ahead of a presidential visit is facing more charges, as authorities released new details about the investigation. Authorities say federal agents first observed 38-year-old Jeanine John Taele near the golf grounds in Rancho Palos Verdes on 31 July, wearing an earpiece and capturing photographs and videos of security agents assessing the property. Taele returned on 2 August, authorities say, two days before Trump was scheduled to visit the resort for a fundraising dinner with the Republican National Committee (RNC). Taele approached federal agents and said he was employed by the state department and was there for a security detail. After detaining Taele for “suspicious” behavior, Los Angeles county sheriff’s deputies found a loaded magazine in his pocket. In his pickup truck, which was parked at the golf club, deputies found a loaded 9mm pistol, binoculars and a badge labeled “security protection agent”, authorities have said. Armed man arrested at Trump’s California golf course Read more Law enforcement officers also recovered a trove of armaments from his residence in the nearby city of Downey, including a .45-caliber pistol, body armor and an illegally modified AR-type pistol, among others, officials said. Law enforcement officials also located notebooks containing “concerning statements” in the home. The Los Angeles county sheriff’s office declined to comment on the nature of the remarks. Taele was due in court on Wednesday on a federal weapons charge but the hearing was canceled. He was charged federally with possession of an unregistered short-barreled rifle that was found at this home, authorities said. The complaint alleges the firearm is an illegally modified AR-style rifle with a barrel that was cut down to 10in (25cm) from 14in (35cm). He is being held at a downtown Los Angeles jail on state charges, according to booking records. He was not yet in federal custody, said a spokesperson for the US attorney’s office. Taele is facing a misdemeanor charge for carrying a concealed weapon in a vehicle and two felony charges for possession of a short-barreled rifle or shotgun and the manufacture, importation or sale of a large-capacity magazine, court records show. The Los Angeles county public defender’s office, which is representing Taele in the state criminal case, declined to comment. Trump addressed the arrest on Tuesday, telling Fox News that “only consequential presidents” are targeted, “and I am definitely consequential”, which he said brought him “a little solace”. Taele already appeared in court on state weapons charges and a second-degree robbery charge for an unrelated incident. “There is no room for error, particularly in light of previous attempts on President Trump’s life,” said Patrick Grandy, the assistant director in charge of the FBI’s Los Angeles office, in a statement. In April, Cole Tomas Allen, a California man who authorities say harbored resentment for the Trump administration, rushed past a security checkpoint during the White House correspondents’s association dinner, where the president was in attendance, and shot a firearm before being apprehended by Secret Service agents. He has been charged with an attempt to assassinate a US president, to which he has pleaded not guilty . In July 2024, a gunman opened fire at a rally where Trump was speaking as the Republican presidential nominee. A crowd member was killed and a bullet grazed Trump’s ear. Federal agents fatally shot the suspected shooter, 20-year-old Thomas Matthew Crooks. An FBI investigation found no clear motive behind the deadly shooting. Ryan Routh was recently sentenced to life in prison after being convicted of attempting to assassinate Trump on a Florida golf course in September 2024. Prosecutors said Routh spent weeks plotting to kill Trump before aiming a rifle through shrubbery as Trump played golf at his West Palm Beach country club. Taele was a corporal in the US marines who was deployed to Iraq in 2008 and Afghanistan in 2010 and worked as a warehouse clerk, according to the US Marine Corps. He earned numerous commendations, including an award for good conduct, during his service from 2008 to 2016. In October 2016, Taele was issued a California firearm permit for .40-caliber, .45-caliber and 9mm weapons, state records show. That permit expired in 2020. Taele was also a licensed security guard in the state between February 2019 and February 2025, records show. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c770.text: By Emma Pengelly Â and Â Richard Irvine-Brown ,Â BBC Verify Published 8 hours ago More than 900 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza this year despite the ceasefire, according to latest figures from the territory's Hamas-run Ministry of Health. It brings the total number of Palestinians killed in the Strip since the 10 October ceasefire was declared to more than 1,300, including 301 children, the ministry says. Hamas and Israel agreed to halt the war after accepting US President Donald Trump's 20-point peace plan. That plan included a suspension of "all military operations, including aerial and artillery bombardment". Since then, BBC Verify has analysed dozens of videos which show the impact of Israeli strikes on locations including a beachside cafe, tents where displaced people have been sheltering, and a reported funeral procession in central Gaza. Recent months have been some of the most deadly according to the figures, with more than 100 people recorded killed each month between April and August. The health ministry attributes the deaths directly to Israeli military action, but does not distinguish between civilians and combatants. The UN considers the figures reliable, and experts have told BBC Verify that their independent analysis is consistent with the ministry's data. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) disputes the ministry's figures. It told BBC Verify there is "no basis to assume" that all those listed were killed as a result of IDF activity. It said it operates in "a precise manner to remove threats and protect its troops and Israeli civilians, in accordance with the agreement", and that it works to mitigate any civilian harm "to the greatest extent possible". At the start of this year Israeli media reported that an Israeli security official acknowledged more than 70,000 people had been killed in the Gaza war, which it said included more than 20,000 combatants. 'Ceasefire in name only' From the start of the ceasefire agreement on 10 October to the end of that month, the ministry recorded 251 deaths. Since then the deadly Israeli attacks have continued every month. The highest monthly death toll this year was recorded in July, when 152 people were killed including 21 children, according to the figures. The IDF says five of its soldiers have been killed in combat since the ceasefire and one contractor was killed in an "operational accident". It also says it has killed hundreds of military operatives since October. Conflict monitoring group Armed Conflict Location and Event Data (Acled), which uses official statements, media reports and social media to verify attacks, says it has recorded around 200 Israeli strikes during the ceasefire that have reportedly killed Hamas operatives or other armed "militants" in targeted strikes. Acled said this includes commanders involved in planning the Hamas-led 7 October 2023 attack on Israel, which triggered the war and killed around 1,200 people with 251 taken hostage. Hugh Lovatt, senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations think tank, said "Gaza has seen a ceasefire in name only" since last October. He said the Israeli military has continued its almost daily air and drone strikes, and "though it claims to be targeting Hamas or imminent threats, it is Gaza's civilians that have continued to bear the brunt". This could now be a "central stumbling block" in international efforts to implement Trump's ceasefire deal, he added. The IDF told BBC Verify it "remains committed" to the ceasefire agreement and that there have been "continued violations and threats posed by Hamas and other terror organizations" in Gaza. Summer of deadly incidents Warning: The following segment of this story contains graphic content which some readers might find distressing. Figure caption, Multiple deadly Israeli strikes in Gaza in under 24 hours BBC Verify has analysed dozens of videos of attacks in Gaza carried out since the ceasefire. In one, emergency services are seen attending to people in the aftermath of a strike at a beachside cafe in Gaza City on 18 August, where six people were killed, according to the health ministry. The next day nine people, including a 13-year-old, were reportedly killed in a strike on a police headquarters in the al-Tuffah neighbourhood. The IDF said it was targeting Hamas commanders and terrorists in the two incidents and that "steps were taken to mitigate harm to civilians". One of the deadliest single incidents in July was a strike on a reported funeral procession in Nuseirat. Seven people were killed and 22 injured, according to the Al-Awda Hospital where casualties were taken. Several verified images show nine people covered in blood lying on the street. Two people appear to still be alive and are being treated by bystanders. The IDF said it was targeting a "significant military operative" of the Palestinian Islamic Jihad group who was involved in the 7 October 2023 attacks. Image source, Supplied Image caption, Men assess scene of Israeli strike on high-rise block in Gaza City on 2 August In a strike on an apartment block on the western edge of Gaza City overnight on 1 August, a pregnant woman, her husband and their young son were killed, according to local reports. Verified footage showed the body of an unborn baby in the rubble. A man searching the ruins said he had heard a strike overnight and saw smoke coming from the building. "I broke the door and went up and I found dead bodies scattered," he said. The IDF said it had targeted an acting Hamas commander. Child deaths 'absurd and devastating' UN agency Unicef has also reported more than 300 children have been killed since the ceasefire. The aid organisation has been tracking all available reports of incidents affecting children in Gaza, including via UN personnel on the ground. James Elder, Unicef global spokesperson, said the number of child deaths was "absurd and devastating". He added that hundreds more have been injured. "A ceasefire that paints such a grim picture can only be failing children." Unicef and other humanitarian organisations operating inside Gaza have also reported Israeli strikes on their workers since the ceasefire. This includes two water truck drivers contracted by Unicef killed in April by Israeli fire at the Mansoura water filling point in northern Gaza. The IDF said its soldiers "identified suspects approaching" the Yellow Line area during the incident, who were later identified as UN contractors who had not "coordinated in advance". Unicef said the drivers were carrying out routine water trucking operations with "no changes in movement or procedures". Aid Worker Security Database, whose figures have been cited by the UN and UK government, told BBC Verify it has recorded 22 aid workers killed in Gaza since 10 October 2025. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Palestinians grieve over bodies of people killed in an Israeli attack targeting a beachfront cafe in Gaza City Independent research group Airwars works to identify civilian deaths from a range of open sources including news agencies, NGOs and social media, matching names it finds to those published by the health ministry. Director Emily Tripp told BBC Verify the ministry's data on death tolls is consistent with its own tracking and research, and that it recorded more than 60 deadly incidents in July. "This is the highest number of fatal incidents we've seen in a month since the ceasefire," Tripp said. "Our own findings point to an increasing number of civilian harm incidents a month." How the dead are counted in Gaza Published 16 November 2023 Professor Michael Spagat from Royal Holloway, University of London, is the chair of Every Casualty Counts, a charity that studies death tolls in wars. He told BBC Verify that the figures recorded by the health ministry are "testable" because it publishes names, ages and ID numbers of the dead. He said that since April, the monthly death toll in Gaza has been roughly double what was seen in December. "July was the worst month but even August's lower toll is still high compared with the November to March period," he added. https://www.politico.eu/article/nvidia-h.text: Nvidia hired law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead an investigation into reports that CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang was the target of a Chinese intelligence operation. Law firm partner Joon H. Kim will lead the probe. Kim, a former acting attorney of the Southern District of New York, was appointed in 2021 as an independent investigator by New York Attorney General Letitia James to probe allegations of sexual harassment by former Gov. Andrew Cuomo. The company’s board of directors on Sunday launched an independent investigation into Jensen Huang following reports of his romantic relationship with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy. The board said that Jensen Huang supports the review. Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang was first brought to light in an October New York Times report , which alleged the businesswoman had ties to Chinese intelligence. Officials suspected Alice Huang helped funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China, according to the report. Jensen Huang in a message to the company Sunday admitted to an affair and pledged to cooperate with the investigation. He did not mention Alice Huang by name. Advertisement Advertisement

https://enrsi.stvr.sk/articles/news/4666.text: Representatives of the Slovak Nuclear Energy Company (JESS) and US company Westinghouse on Wednesday signed a contract for the provision of preliminary project engineering services in connection with the new nuclear power facility in Jaslovske Bohunice. After the signing of the contract, Prime Minister Robert Fico (Smer-SD) admitted that the project had been delayed by eight to ten months. However, he believes that nothing will stop the process now. The new unit is to be rated at 1,100 megawatts (MW), whereas a capacity of 1,200 MW had previously been discussed, said Fico. As he told the US partners, he wants to make sure that the project preparation process becomes irreversible even after the 2027 elections. According to Westinghouse Senior Vice President Elias Gedeon, the company wants to start working on the study the very next day so that the Slovak government and JESS could get the necessary information as soon as possible in order to move on to the next steps. "We look forward to working with Slovak suppliers as well, and not only as regards the Jaslovske Bohunice project," added Gedeon. According to Fico's previous statements, a contract for the construction of the nuclear power plant could be signed in 2027, while the new nuclear facility could be commissioned by 2040 at the site of the existing nuclear power plant in Jaslovske Bohunice (Trnava region). Source: TASR
